text_blocks.snippet: A COVID-19 breakthrough infection is defined as a SARS-CoV-2 infection that occurs in a fully vaccinated individual, meaning 14 days after receiving all recommended doses of an authorized vaccine. These infections are relatively common, particularly with the Omicron variant, and can be attributed to factors like vaccine effectiveness, individual characteristics, and the virus itself. While breakthrough infections can occur, they are often less severe, with fewer hospitalizations and less morbidity, according to BMC Infectious Diseases.
